subject: Re: Throughput degradation in Dedicated pool — remediation plan and credits
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.m@stellar-analytics.com>
Cc: Elena Cruz <e.cruz@stellar-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: [Incident] Notice: Throughput degradation on Dedicated GPU pool (us-west-2)

Hi Jordan,

We’re writing to let you know we’re seeing a sustained degradation in throughput for a subset of requests served from Dedicated pools in us-west-2 that may impact latency and token throughput for your reserved capacity.

What we know so far:
- Window: 2026-11-02 08:54–09:10 UTC (ongoing at the time of this message).
- Symptoms: increased queuing and token latency for long-context generation jobs; autoscale did not engage as expected for some reserved nodes.
- Affected: a small number of Dedicated pools; we believe Stellar Analytics’ reserved pool is within the impacted cohort.

Immediate mitigations we have enacted:
- Manual node rebalancing to reduce queue depth for your pool.
- Increased short-term burst capacity while we identify the root cause.
- Opened an incident bridge (details below) and escalated to SRE and Runtime teams.

Next steps we are taking:
1) Full trace and kernel selection analysis (SRE + Runtime) — ETA 4–6 hours.
2) If autoscale behavior is determined to be the issue, we will push a configuration patch and run a controlled rollout.
3) We will provide a post-incident summary and remediation timeline within 72 hours, including any service credit proposal if SLA targets were missed.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (short timeline stub), we’ll follow with a formal postmortem doc.

I’ll keep you updated on the bridge. If you’d like us to join a quick call now, I can loop in the SRE lead.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:40:12 -0000
Subject: Internal: Incident INF-7234 — root cause, impact, and proposed credit

Team — quick internal summary (for the record):
- Root cause (preliminary): regression in kernel selection heuristics that underestimates memory pressure for long-context LLMs, which prevented autoscale from triggering on some Dedicated nodes and caused queue head-of-line blocking.
- Impact: approx. 7% of reserved pools in us-west-2 experienced >2x token latency for 16–32 token windows; 3 customers reported timeouts on production batch jobs (including Stellar Analytics).
- Mitigation taken: manual node rebalance + forced autoscale override + rolling patch to kernel selector.

Proposed customer remediation for affected accounts:
- 10% service credit for the affected window for customers with SLA (pending legal sign-off).
- Technical follow-up: detailed postmortem + configuration guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Please confirm approval to offer the credit and the postmortem link I’ll send to customers. I’m drafting the external message now.

—Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.m@stellar-analytics.com>, Elena Cruz <e.cruz@stellar-analytics.com>, procurement@stellar-analytics.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: [Postmortem] Dedicated pool throughput degradation — summary and next steps

Jordan / Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the investigation. Below is the concise post-incident summary for INF-7234 and the actions Redwood will take for Stellar Analytics.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-11-02 08:54–09:10 UTC. Root cause: a kernel-selection regression introduced in the runtime’s 4.8.2 deploy that misclassified memory pressure for certain long-context models, which led to reduced autoscale triggers and queue head-of-line blocking.
- Impact to Stellar Analytics: transient token latency increases and timeouts on some batch jobs. We confirmed customer success impact on three production jobs you identified and validated traces matching our kernel-selection signature.

What we fixed and why it prevents recurrence:
- Reverted the offending heuristic and rolled kernel-selection patch 4.8.3 with additional unit tests.
- Added a guardrail: autoscale will now run a secondary validation pass for memory pressure before skipping scale decisions.
- Improved telemetry: new per-pool memory-pressure histograms and alerting to detect the pattern earlier.

Compensation and next steps for Stellar Analytics:
- We will issue a 10% service credit for the affected time window. Attached: service_credit_voucher.pdf (billing team will apply against Nov invoice).
- We invite your SREs to a technical deep-dive with our runtime engineers to review kernel selection and telemetry — proposed slots linked here: https://cal.com/redwood/runtime-deep-dive.
- Full postmortem document: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-redwood-postmortems/stellar-4482 and attached redwood_dedicated_postmortem_v1.pdf.

If you’d like us to set up the deep-dive or you want additional context for procurement, I can loop in our contracts team.

Apologies for the impact — we take SLA commitments seriously and appreciate your partnership as we improve.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
